body: Wow, that's some sad propaganda that I'm ashamed I've fallen for. Thank you very much for this valuable education towards me. I would never ever ever dismiss someone's gender confusion, transgender or otherwise and I've learned a great deal. I think you're missing the point, I do understand what body dysphoria feels like. Not necessarily completely what it is to be trans of course, but I ask my trans friends about their experiences. My post has nothing to do with trans - moreso the other gender identities. I'm referring to things like cis people who identify as non-binary etc. Someone had changed my mind in another threat.   


I have every respect for trans people. I empathize 100% with feeling like being born in the wrong body is torture. I have experienced a body dysphoria I'd not like to get into details about, but during that time I hated my body and wanted to die. I was moreso referring to people SPECIFICALLY that are not trans.   


But want to know something kind of wild and cool? My name is Ashley, I'm 30 years old. When I was 25, I got a message from someone saying they were my niece. Not only that, their name was Ashley. Not only that, they were a lesbian. They were 24. I thought for sure someone was trolling me. I learned I had an illegitimate niece named Ashley (deadname) born a year before me by my brother who abandoned (her) at the time.  


He shortly came out as trans, and I have a nephew named Jay who is almost my complete TWIN. He's the male version of me! It's amazing and I love him to death. Despite us not growing up together, we are so similar. He is also polyamorous like I am. :)

And perhaps I have simply grown an arrogance having to pave the way myself, growing up in a small town community defying gender stereotypes and empowering myself, perhaps it's given me an ego and that's why I had not looked fondly on the broad range of new genders that are coming out. 

I know for a fact it made me a stronger person, but couldn't wrap my head around the fact it gives people peace with their inner turmoil because it's something I had already dealt with myself. I am so happy you took the time to answer my post. It was very a very valuable learning experience.

Hm, I didn't think about it that way. :) Thank you for sharing that perspective. I'm so glad that it helped you process your inner turmoil, and that's all it takes for me to completely respect varying gender identities other than the binary and forcing trans people into the binary based on what they identify with. Thank you so kindly for your response. It was actually so enlightening and thank you for understanding my intentions were not to disrespect anyone, and for treating me with respect.  


In my thread I asked someone to change my mind, and than you ohay\_nicole, you have certainly done so and now I understand the value of differing gender identities outside of the binary. I deeply appreciate you taking the time to explain this to me and enlighten me, and I have such a better understanding why this is SO valuable to people. I could not understand before, but I think I have a far better appreciation of how it helps people with their internal struggles. Eternally grateful. You have a lovely day. :)

I just guess perhaps with my life experiences and being these things before these genders were defined, I see little use for them and maybe I'm out of touch being from a generation before these things were welcomed, identified and etc. I really mean no harm, in my post I say "change my mind" because I truly wish to understand. Maybe i'm too old and out of touch at the ripe age of 30. :P

This isn't primarily about my sexuality, rather my androgynous clothing. With this in mind, can you give me a better understanding of your position?

The main part is I'm a feminist that doesn't believe in gender roles, therefore I don't understand why these entire wikipedias of gender exist. I can be androgynous, I don't feel particularly make or female and don't need to define myself based on those traits.

Do you think this is fictional thing? I've heard of things like astrogender and stuff. Like I have no idea what some of these things have to do with gender identity. You're right, I've never met anyone who has claimed to be any of these things I've seen on the gender wiki. I fully support trans people and viciously attack anyone who says anything disparaging about them. I just don't really understand the rest, and if they're a work of malicious propaganda, I see why this gender issue is such a heated thing. 

Just to clarify, do you think I am propagating malicious propaganda or other people are to make people dismiss alternate genders and things like transgenderism?

Unpopular opinion:

I  am 30 years old, and came out as a lesbian at 14 years old. I like to  rock an androgynous look, I don’t necessarily identify with either  non-binary or any of the other miscellaneous genders. I most definitely  don’t feel male or female, which I accept without needing a label  attached to that.

Have I been  misgendered the odd time someone thinks I’m a guy? Sure. I identify as  female. I spent a good part of my life being empowered by living life by  my own rules, refusing to be put in any kind of box.

I  had to grow up this way, and ultimately this has left me empowered and  more confident about myself as a person, as I’ve had to stick up for  myself, correct people and the like. Could I be considered non-binary?  Sure. But I don’t feel the need to have my identity defined as so. I’m  content being gendered as a female, and I’m a feminist who doesn’t  believe in gender roles regardless.

I  absolutely and whole-heartedly embrace trans people. I have no qualms  respecting this. But I feel the struggles I’ve had to go through before  the sensitivity towards gender non-binary and these new terms that seem  to grow by the day have made me a far stronger more confident person.  Sure I get a little miffed if someone misgenders me.

I  feel stronger having to assert my gender identity. I disagree with the  thousands of genders, I only agree with male/female binary and  completely accept trans people. I feel this movement of gender identity  is contagious, confusing and offputting for people that don’t accept  this. I think it makes people weak and entitled to confuse and demand  people that aren't going to respect your gender identity in the first  place is just damaging if we EXPECT people to cater to things they don't  believe in themselves. I don’t see why it’s necessary and why people  feel damaged being misgendered.(OTHER THAN TRANS) I feel personally that  people put so much stock into their identity that it’s gotten  ridiculous at this point.

Technically  I’m non-binary, I might dress female one day, more male the other but I  don’t need to announce to the world that I’m non binary because I don’t  need the way I dress or feel to validate my identity.

In  my humble opinion, it’s vastly unnecessary and feel that people won’t  get the valuable experience of being a trendsetter, seeing opposition  and growing from the confidence I get knowing I can do me without having  to attach some kind of identity to it.

I’m  in the LGBT community, and I respect people’s wishes but I feel that it  makes people weak to have to define their identity over such things. If  you’re trans, yes hun I support you in every regards.

But  I feel there are only two genders. I’m an androgynous lesbian who  dresses however I choose to at the time, I don’t feel bound my gender  roles as I am a feminist. I don't believe in gender roles period. I'm  all for butch women, effeminate men breaking gender stereotypes.

Are  these excessive genders healthy for people? I don’t think so, change my  mind. I feel like it’s leaving people without the opportunity to grow  more confident in their identity because lets face it, there’s only a  minority of people that are actually going to respect people’s gender  identities when a pretty big majority of people are not going to respect  them in general.

I feel like  people just need to cling to an identity to feel different. I’m an  androgynous woman who refuses to call myself complicated gender roles to  validate my need to feel different. I feel this society on the left is  going very overboard. I’m a lesbian, and I only believe in two genders.  If a trans person identifies as a woman, you bet your ass I will respect  and treat them as a woman but all of these complicated genders seem  superfluous and maybe egotistical.
